ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT Act) and Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (Definitions) Regulations 2011; Companies Act 1993, including section 87 (shareholder register) and section 190 (registered office); Terrorism Suppression Act 2002 and Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009; regulatory and supervisory coordination by the Financial Markets Authority, Reserve Bank of New Zealand, and Department of Internal Affairs; New Zealand has no public UBO register, but reporting entities must identify and verify beneficial owners to PM/FIU standards.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office / Registrar of Companies
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route (for Apostille Convention destination states): notarize the original document and obtain an Apostille from the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT) Authentication Unit. Consular Legalization route (for non-member destination states): instead present the notarized document to the destination state's embassy/consulate in New Zealand for legalization. The two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain them.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Compliance)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office / Registrar of Companies
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: notarize and obtain an MFAT Apostille. Consular Legalization route: notarize and submit to the destination jurisdiction's consular post in New Zealand. Use only one authentication path depending on the destination state's status; do not combine apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Board Resolution of the First Directors Authorizing Incorporation, Banking and Execution of Powers of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered legal counsel / New Zealand notary public on behalf of NZ LTD
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: notarize the executed board resolution and obtain an MFAT Apostille. Consular Legalization route: notarize the resolution and have it legalized by the receiving state's consulate in New Zealand. The two routes are alternative, not cumulative.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Company Constitution) of NZ LTD
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand law firm / founding shareholder resolution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: notarize a certified copy of the constitution and obtain an MFAT Apostille. Consular Legalization route: after notarization, apply for consular legalization at the destination state's embassy/consulate. Do not stack apostille after consular legalization or vice versa.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter / Comfort Letter for the Ultimate Beneficial Owner and Proposed NZ LTD
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand registered bank or the applicant's overseas bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: notarize the bank's signed letter and obtain an MFAT Apostille. Consular Legalization route: if the destination country is not an Apostille member, the notarized letter must be legalized by that country's consulate in New Zealand. Use only the route required by the destination country.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must cover every beneficial owner, director, and authorized signatory against the New Zealand Sanctions Act lists, the United Nations Consolidated List, and the OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists where any USD payment rail or US nexus exists. Screening must also include HM Treasury/UK and EU consolidated sanctions where relevant, global politically exposed person (PEP) databases, adverse media and negative news alerts, bankruptcy and regulatory disqualification records, and the New Zealand Companies Office corporate register. Full UBO tracing must be performed to every natural person holding at least 25% ownership or control, with enhanced due diligence applied to high-risk jurisdictions and required suspicious activity reporting to the New Zealand Financial Intelligence Unit under section 40 of the AML/CFT Act.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office (Companies Register) - register.companiesoffice.govt.nz
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Companies Act 1993 and Companies Office Name Registration Guidelines, company names must use Latin-alphabet characters; te reo Maori names are permissible in Latin script with macrons. Non-Latin names require phonetic transliteration into the Latin alphabet. The four-tier naming convention applies: exact legal name, phonetic transliteration, translated name, and abbreviated trading name. The approved registered name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing company, reserved name, or protected name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant has 20 working days to file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar of Companies through the Companies Office portal, attaching the rejection notice, a statutory justification, and any ministerial consent or evidence of non-confusion. The Registrar must issue a reasoned decision. If the rejection is upheld, the applicant may initiate judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand under the Judicature Amendment Act 1972 within 28 days of the final decision, and may concurrently seek an interim order to preserve the name during the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: New Zealand law requires every company to maintain a registered office in New Zealand (Companies Act 1993, section 190). A virtual office or commercial mailbox may satisfy the Companies Office address requirement, but Inland Revenue and New Zealand banks generally reject a virtual-only arrangement as the principal place of business for manufacturing activities such as polyresin vacuum casting and hand-painted statue production. For this industry, the entity should maintain a physical production, warehousing, or serviced manufacturing site; a virtual office can only supplement substance and cannot be the sole operational address for GST registration, environmental compliance, or bank account opening.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) physical signboard at the registered office; (2) access to board minute books and share register; (3) evidence of production equipment, molds, resin inventory, and painting tools; (4) GST returns and sales invoices; (5) payroll and health and safety records; (6) local council zoning and resource consent for resin casting; (7) hazardous waste disposal contracts. Quantified risk: low-to-moderate for a genuinely operating manufacturing site (approximately 30% probability of an unannounced IRD, Companies Office, or municipal inspection within the first 24 months); the risk rises above 60% if the registered office is a virtual mailbox and no physical production address is verifiable.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), including sections 5 (name), 16 (registration), 18 (certificate of incorporation), 33-35 (directors and consent to act), 42 (registered office), 50 (allotment of shares), 83 (register of directors), 126 (annual returns), and 189 (service of documents)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (online incorporation form) filed through the New Zealand Companies Office proprietary register
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Companies Act 1993. A New Zealand limited company has no statutory minimum paid-up capital requirement, no escrow account requirement, and no initial capital deposit obligation. The company must, however, have at least one shareholder and at least one director resident in New Zealand or Australia, and share capital must be fully or partly paid or supported by an enforceable subscription agreement. The board must ensure the share register accurately records all issued shares and consideration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [●] LIMITED (the Company), duly held on [●] 2025 at the registered office of the Company, at [●], New Zealand. Notice was waived by all directors. The Chairperson declared a quorum present. After lawful deliberation, the Board unanimously adopted the following resolutions: 1. REGISTERED OFFICE AND SERVICE AGENT: That the registered office of the Company shall be established at [●], New Zealand, and the Board hereby adopts the same for all statutory communications. The Board appoints the directors and any company secretary as the authorised agents for service of legal process pursuant to section 188 of the Companies Act 1993. 2. SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT OF SHARES: That the initial allotment of ordinary shares in the Company as recorded in the share register is hereby ratified, confirmed and approved. The Board acknowledges receipt of the capital contribution, or the enforceable subscription undertaking, set out in the subscription agreement. The directors are instructed to issue share certificates and to file relevant returns with the Registrar of Companies. 3. BANKING AUTHORIZATIONS: That [●] Bank, [●] branch, is appointed as the Company's principal banker. The Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer, acting jointly, shall operate the bank accounts, sign cheques, authorise wire transfers, issue mandates and execute banking security documents. Any single officer transaction above [●] shall require prior approval of the Board. 4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS: That the following officers are appointed: [●] as Chief Executive Officer, [●] as Company Secretary, and [●] as Chief Financial Officer. The Company Secretary shall ensure maintenance of all statutory registers, preparation of annual returns, and compliance with filing deadlines. The officers hold office at the pleasure of the Board and have all powers delegated in accordance with the Companies Act 1993 and the Company's constitution. 5. CORPORATE GOVERNANCE DELEGATION: That the draft constitution presented to this meeting is adopted as the Company's constitution. The officers are authorised to apply to Inland Revenue for the New Zealand Business Number and IRD number, register for GST where appropriate, and open the Companies Office and myIR online services. 6. INDEMNITIES AND EFFECTIVE DATE: That all incorporation expenses and service fees are ratified, and the Company will indemnify the officers and directors to the extent permitted by law. These resolutions are effective immediately and may be relied upon by third parties until revoked.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Director Eligibility Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Online Name Reservation portal, MBIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Utilize the 'Apply to Reserve a Company Name' facility on the New Zealand Companies Office register operated by the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment. Input the proposed corporate name, select 'Limited' or 'Ltd' as the legal suffix, and declare the intended company type. Conduct a preliminary search for conflicting names, existing registered trademarks, and prohibited expressions. Submit a formal name reservation application together with a short business description covering the manufacture of polyresin statues. Pay the prescribed reservation fee and await the automated approval. If the company name contains a restricted word, upload the written consent of the relevant authority. The applicant's passport or national identity card must be certified or notarized when the applicant is a non-resident.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and legal suffix
Passport or national ID of the applicant
Written consent for any restricted word (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to phonetic or visual similarity, refine the name and re-apply. If the reservation expires before incorporation, reserve a fresh name. The applicant may also file a notice with the Companies Office explaining any special circumstances or apply for a non-distinctive name review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Governing Constitution, Consents, and Share Subscription Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Formation counsel in coordination with New Zealand Companies Office (no filing at this step)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The formation attorney prepares the company constitution in accordance with the Companies Act 1993, including authorised share capital, share classes, transfer restrictions, director powers, indemnity, and notice provisions. All proposed directors must execute written consents to act, declaring that they are permitted to be directors and not disqualified. The shareholders must execute a share subscription agreement setting out the number of shares subscribed and the form of consideration. The registered office address must be a physical New Zealand street address and cannot be a post office box alone. The first accounting period end date and banking mandate instructions should be determined at this stage. All documents must be dated and witnessed. If any director resides outside New Zealand, at least one director must be resident in New Zealand or Australia.
required_dossiers: Signed consent to act for each director
Share subscription agreement and shareholder consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an officer consent form is incomplete, correct and re-execute it. If the Companies Office later challenges an officer's eligibility, submit a statutory declaration and supporting character references. If constitution clauses are ambiguous, the Board may adopt the Companies Act default rules and file an updated constitution by special resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Online Incorporation Filing and Certificate Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (Companies Register online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Companies Office portal using a RealMe verified identity. Select 'Register a Company', input the reserved name reference, director and shareholder particulars, registered address, and upload the constitution and consents. Review the pre-completed application for accuracy and authorise the registration. Pay the state incorporation fee of NZD 150 (approximately USD 88) through the online payment gateway. Once submitted, the Registrar of Companies will verify that all statutory documents are present. Where everything is correct, the Registrar will issue the Certificate of Incorporation and the Companies Register will display the company number and registration date. Download the electronic Companies Extract and preserve the certificate for subsequent bank, tax and licensing applications. The applicant must promptly update the share register and notify initial officers of their appointment.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is pended for clarification, respond in writing to the Companies Office within the stated deadline, typically 10 business days. If the Registrar rejects a document, correct the form and resubmit; if the reserved name had expired, make a fresh name reservation. In exceptional cases, apply for the Registrar to extend the decision period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax Registration, Bank Account Activation, and Initial Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department, New Zealand and a registered New Zealand bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, apply to Inland Revenue for an IRD number and New Zealand Business Number through the Business Registration portal. Register for GST if projected taxable supplies exceed NZD 60,000 per year; register for PAYE and KiwiSaver if employees are to be engaged. Concurrently, open a corporate bank account with an approved New Zealand bank. Provide the certificate of incorporation, constitution, board resolution, directors' identification, proof of residential address, and completed AML/CFT questionnaires. The bank will conduct due diligence and, once the account is active, the directors must deposit initial share capital or record the capital receivable. The officers must also verify that the Companies Register shows the company as Active and update any new directors or registered office changes promptly.
required_dossiers: First board resolution appointing bankers and officers
Director/shareholder certified IDs and address proofs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Inland Revenue needs additional proof, a director may provide original certified documents or attend a RealMe verification. If the bank delays the account, supply a corporate chart and source-of-funds statement. If the capital is not deposited due to cross-border exchange controls, record the subscription receivable and seek fund transfer approval before calling up capital.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: WorkSafe New Zealand; New Zealand Environmental Protection Authority; and the local Territorial Authority (District or City Council) for the manufacturing premises
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Combined Resource Consent for Manufacturing Activity, Building Act 2004 Code Compliance Certificate, and Hazardous Substances Location Certificate

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: New Zealand Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) together with the relevant Regional Council under the Resource Management Act 1991
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Small-scale polyresin vacuum casting and hand-painting is generally a Permitted Activity under regional plans when the annual resin throughput is below 500 kg/year. If the project scales beyond the permitted thresholds, emits significant VOCs, or raises local amenity effects, the operation becomes a Restricted Discretionary Activity requiring an assessment of environmental effects (AEE) and a full resource consent application; the level is Category 2 (moderate environmental impact).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Styrene and volatile organic compound emissions from resin casting must be extracted and treated with at least 95% capture or destruction efficiency. Workplace exposure to styrene must remain below the eight-hour time-weighted average of 20 ppm and the short-term exposure limit of 50 ppm under the Health and Safety at Work (Hazardous Substances) Regulations 2017. Any stack discharge of VOCs must not exceed 100 mg/m3 as a one-hour average. Wastewater from the casting process may only be discharged to the municipal sewer under an approved trade-waste permit, and must meet pH 6.0 to 9.0, total suspended solids below 600 mg/L, and oil and grease below 100 mg/L. No untreated hazardous waste may be released to land, stormwater, or groundwater. Spent resin drums and paints must be stored in bunded containment and removed by a licensed hazardous-waste contractor.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The facility must obtain a Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) fire systems inspection and a civil defense fire safety certificate covering the storage of flammable resins, catalysts, and aerosol paints. Under the Building Act 2004, the premises must carry a Building Code Compliance Certificate based on structural load inspection and fire-rated separation, issued by the local Territorial Authority. WorkSafe New Zealand clearance requires a site-specific workplace safety policy, hazardous substances emergency response plan, chemical inventory, ventilation verification, and staff training records.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Inland Revenue; Te Tari Taake), the national tax authority of New Zealand. Statutory functions and filing are administered through the official portal www.ird.govt.nz, with all tax registrations, GST returns, and secure communications effected through the myIR (myIR Secure Online Services) platform. Company incorporation and the issue of the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) are administered by the New Zealand Companies Office under the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) The NZ_LTD is incorporated under the Companies Act 1993 via the Companies Office online register; the incorporation application automatically issues the NZBN and typically simultaneously registers the company for an IRD number and GST where the taxable-activity declarations are completed. 2) If the company has already been incorporated or was formed without tax registrations, the procuring officer must file IRD Form IR596 (Company IRD Number Application) through the myIR portal; the IRD number is generally issued within 5-10 business days, with an IRD number confirmation letter delivered to the registered addresses. 3) GST registration is compulsory once the value of taxable supplies exceeds NZ$60,000 in any 12-month period; registration is executed via the myIR portal (or the Companies Office new-company workflow) using Form IR356, with the effective GST registration date aligned to the start of the taxable activity or the date of incorporation if the company elects voluntary registration. 4) For a foreign company operating in New Zealand through a branch, the entity must first apply for registration as an overseas company with the Companies Office under Part 18 of the Companies Act 1993 and then obtain an IRD number by filing Form IR596 with certified incorporation documents, registered-office particulars, and a New Zealand service address. For a NZ-incorporated limited company with non-resident shareholders, the company is automatically a tax resident of New Zealand and is not subject to residency elections at incorporation; all statutory tax filings must be made in the IRD number of the NZ_LTD.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — The NZ Limited Company is a separate legal and taxable person. Under s YA 2 of the Income Tax Act 2007, a company incorporated in New Zealand is tax resident in New Zealand and is taxed at the 28% corporate rate on its worldwide income. There is no territorial limitation for resident companies; foreign income is taxable in New Zealand with foreign tax credits available under the foreign tax credit rules, and the full imputation credit system applies to resident and non-resident shareholders to prevent economic double taxation. New Zealand operates a unitary national tax system without state or provincial income taxes. The standard entity-level model is not a pass-through; however, eligible closely held companies may elect Look-Through Company treatment as described below.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: 1) Look-Through Company (LTC) election under subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007: an eligible closely held company (maximum 5 qualifying shareholders, each a natural person, eligible trust or another LTC) may elect full pass-through taxation of its income, expenses, losses, and tax credits to shareholders; the election is binding for 5 years and requires shareholder consent on each qualifying share, without prejudice to GST registration which remains at company level. 2) Non-Resident Company election under s HB 1: a company incorporated in New Zealand that is managed and controlled outside New Zealand may elect to be treated as a non-resident company for income tax purposes, so that only income with a New Zealand source is subject to tax in New Zealand. 3) Hybrid mismatch rules (subparts FA-FH of the Income Tax Act 2007) are mandatory and non-elective; New Zealand companies involved in structured hybrid arrangements must apply neutralizing adjustments to deny deductions or include income in line with BEPS Action 2. 4) GST Grouping election (s 55, Goods and Services Tax Act 1985) and GST Joint Venture election (s 57) allow the NZ_LTD and associated companies to be treated as single GST-registered persons for input tax and output tax purposes. 5) Dividend imputation and non-resident withholding tax elections, including the foreign dividend exemption and available subscribed capital elections, apply where the NZ_LTD has non-resident shareholders receiving distributions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) — a destination-based value-added consumption tax governed by the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, administered by the Inland Revenue Department. GST applies to most supplies of goods and services made in New Zealand by a registered person, to imported goods, and to certain remote services supplied to New Zealand resident consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZ$60,000 — compulsory GST registration applies to every person carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand where the value of taxable supplies made in New Zealand in any 12-month period exceeds NZ$60,000 (excluding GST). The NZ_LTD is required to register from commencement of its taxable activity once this turnover threshold is reached; voluntary registration below the threshold is permitted and is often elected where input tax credits on establishment costs are material.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: There is no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, no compulsory digital stamping, and no tax-authority clearance-before-issue model in New Zealand. The IRD operates a self-assessment compliance system with periodic GST returns filed through myIR (monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly accounting periods). Electronic invoicing (e-invoicing) is voluntary in the private sector, with the Government promoting the PEPPOL e-invoicing standard for B2B and B2G interoperability; invoices to New Zealand government departments must be transmitted via the Peppol network, but non-government trade can lawfully use paper, PDF, or any other format that satisfies the content requirements of s 24 of the GST Act 1985 (supplier name and GST number, invoice date and number, customer name and address, description of the goods, GST-exclusive amount, GST amount and total consideration). The New Zealand Customs Service requires electronic export declarations in the Trade Single Window portal, which serves as the operational clearance mechanism for exported resin statue goods; GST refunds on export supplies are effected through the ordinary GST return system with IRD payment of net refunds typically made within 10-15 working days.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under s 11(1) of the GST Act 1985, the supply of goods is zero-rated where the supplier has exported the goods from New Zealand within 28 days of the date of supply. For the NZ_LTD's polyresin vacuum-cast and hand-painted limited-edition statues, zero-rating requires that the statues are delivered to a non-resident purchaser or to the purchaser's overseas designee and physically leave New Zealand within the 28-day window; legal title and risk must pass to the overseas buyer under the agreed Incoterms. The supply is not zero-rated if the goods remain in New Zealand, are not exported within 28 days, or are consumed in New Zealand. Exported statue supplies must be recorded as zero-rated in the GST return, and the underlying purchase order (received via Preorder_Deposit_Stripe or PayPal), the export invoice, and the carrier's evidence must demonstrate the overseas destination of each physical consignment. Invoices may be issued in foreign currency for export transactions; for GST return purposes the foreign-currency amount is converted to New Zealand dollars using the IRD's prescribed exchange rate. Services supplied to non-residents outside New Zealand at the time of supply are also zero-rated under s 11A, subject to exceptions for services connected with land, goods, or taxable activities physically performed in New Zealand. The use of Stripe or PayPal payment rails does not by itself alter the export zero-rating analysis, but complete payment and shipping records are essential to satisfy audit evidence requirements.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: NZ Customs Export Declaration (electronic lodgment via the Trade Single Window, message set IE515)
Bill of Lading (sea freight) or Air Waybill (air freight) evidencing shipment from a New Zealand port or airport

Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank foreign-exchange settlement advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds (New Zealand has no statutory exchange-control mandate; this evidence serves as the export-payment verification)
Commercial Invoice and Packing List (overseas consignee address, Incoterms, description of the resin statues and unit values)
Proof of physical export within 28 days of supply (port of loading certificate, container tracking report, sailing or flight departure confirmation, and Customs clearance certificate)
GST zero-rated export schedule and reconciliation supporting the relevant period filed in myIR
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The zero-rating status is retrospective: if goods are not physically exported within 28 days of supply, or are diverted to the New Zealand market, the supplier must return GST at 15% on the supply price and file an adjustment in the relevant GST period. Wrongful zero-rating triggers the shortfall penalty provisions of Part 9 of the Tax Administration Act 1994, together with use-of-money interest: 20% of the tax shortfall for failure to exercise reasonable care, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion, with criminal liability for tax evasion arising under s 143A of the Tax Administration Act 1994 and s 260 of the Crimes Act 1961. The IRD and the New Zealand Customs Service operate joint data-matching of export declarations, freight forwarder records, bill-of-lading data, and banking and payment settlement flows; fully documented and auditable export dossiers are required. Retrospective adjustments and GST clawbacks may be assessed within the 4-year limitation period of s 108 of the Tax Administration Act 1994, with no time limit where evasion or fraudulent intent is established. The 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline reflected in this schema is not a statutory requirement in New Zealand, as the country's exchange controls were abolished in 1984; however, prolonged non-receipt of export proceeds beyond 180 days may be treated as evidence that the export transaction was not genuine and may lead to reassessment of the zero-rating, with the anti-avoidance rule in s 76 of the GST Act 1985 authorizing the Commissioner of Inland Revenue to adjust the GST consequences of any arrangement that defeats the object and purpose of the zero-rating rules.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) as the central monetary and prudential authority; the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) and the Department of Internal Affairs as co-supervisors of the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AMLCFT); the Overseas Investment Office (OIO) under the Ministry for Business, Innovation and Employment as the administrator of New Zealand’s overseas investment screening regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains a fully open capital account and a freely convertible New Zealand dollar under the IMF Article VIII obligations. Both current account and capital account transactions are unrestricted, with no foreign exchange controls, no requirement for central bank approval or no permitted threshold on cross-border capital flows. Profit remittance via dividends, management fees, royalty and intercompany loan repayments to non-resident shareholders is permitted, subject to standard tax withholding at source (e.g. Non-Resident Withholding Tax on dividends and Approved Issuer Levy on interest) and to transfer pricing and beneficial ownership documentation.  The practical hurdles are not exchange control but rather: (i) bank-level KYC/AML diligence on the origin of inbound capital, (ii) the application of the overseas investment screening rules if a substantial asset or shareholding is acquired, and (iii) the statistical balance-of-payments reporting obligations on banks. There is no separate profit remittance licence or fee.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. New Zealand does not impose mandatory export proceeds surrender, conversion ratios, or any statutory timeline for repatriation of export receipts. Exporters may retain foreign currency receipts in offshore or onshore foreign currency accounts, settle in any currency agreed with the buyer, and convert at quotable market rates. The only ancillary compliance obligations are (i) ensuring the underlying export transaction is accurately declared to the New Zealand Customs Service for statistical and tariff purposes, (ii) reflecting the transaction in the exporter’s financial statements and tax returns where applicable, and (iii) preserving underlying commercial invoices, logistics documents and settlement records to support bank KYC/AML checks and any future queries from the Reserve Bank or the New Zealand Customs Service.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. New Zealand does not have a standalone electronic money institution (EMI) licence. A non-bank fintech may provide payment services and hold settlement funds only if it is registered on the Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 and, where applicable, holds a money service business registration that is subject to AMLCFT oversight. Additionally, if the fintech accepts deposits or lends, it must be registered as a bank under the Banking Prudential Supervision Act 1989. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g. Wise Platform, Airwallex, Currencycloud-style aggregators) can provide NZD-denominated virtual accounts, payment disbursements and collection services via a white-label partnership with a licensed New Zealand bank, but they cannot accept deposits or act as the principal holding bank for a commercial entity without a locally registered NZ entity and a local banking partner. Therefore, for the NZ_LTD treasury, an offshore digital EMI is viable as an auxiliary cross-border payment and disbursement rail, but the primary liquidity clearing and escrow relationship must sit with a licensed Tier 1 commercial bank to ensure transactional integrity, credit support and regulatory coverage.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand AMLCFT obligations mandate a risk-based customer due diligence process, and the practical onboarding procedures at Tier 1 banks are rigorous. Most New Zealand banks require a physical or live video-verified interview with at least one director and ideally the principal shareholder and any signing authority; remote online onboarding is increasingly available for low-risk entities with acceptable electronic identity verification (e.g. biometric passport and underlying commercial registry database checks). For a newly incorporated NZ_LTD with non-resident directors, the standard accepted approach is a video interview supplemented by in-person verification of each director or signatory at a New Zealand branch, or alternatively verification by a New Zealand-registered law firm or accounting firm acting as an authorised introducer under the bank’s guidelines. The bank will also require a board resolution authorising account opening, specimen signatures, proof of address of the entity and directors, and a certified copy of the Companies Office (New Zealand) registration certificate. A pure remote onboarding with no meeting or no independent introducer verification is usually only permitted when the entity, owners, suppliers and counterparties are all in low-risk jurisdictions and the product is standard, which is not fully guaranteed for cross-border resin trade.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction or related-party exposure involving a beneficial owner, supplier or counterparty that is subject to enhanced suspicion (e.g. settlement through untransparent payment corridors).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Company registration extracts and certified UBO declarations; copy of the corporate tree and ultimate beneficial owner chart; source of funds statement supported by 12 months of bank statements from the investor’s home bank; original cross-border sales contracts, purchase orders, supplier invoices, shipping and customs documentation; a sworn affidavit from the directors explaining the commercial purpose of each transaction; and an independent legal opinion confirming the absence of sanctions exposure and the beneficial ownership chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in the shareholding or control structure due to trust-held shares, family partnerships or non-resident nominee arrangements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notified board resolution explaining the control structure; certified trust deed or partnership agreement; full register of members with individual identities and citizenship; certified passports and proof of residential address; source of wealth records including professional CVs, property or business sale agreements and tax records; and a notarised statement confirming the natural-person beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual initial capital funding or large prepayment deposit flows that appear inconsistent with a newly established resin statue entity (e.g. sudden receipt of customer pre-order deposits from offshore e-commerce platforms in excess of the invoice value).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital subscription agreement and bank debit/credit entries traceable to the registered issuing of shares; platform settlement reports from Stripe and PayPal showing buyer UBO, payer identity, product SKU and transaction volumes; refund policy and customer terms; product-market proof including catalogues, Etsy/Shopify storefronts or contractual purchase agreements; and a reconciled ledger of customer preorder recibos against manufacturing cost estimates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid outbound wire transfers to suppliers in a different risk jurisdiction from the buyer (e.g. manufacturing in China while customers are in the Americas), raising transaction-velocity mismatches.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trade finance file with proforma invoices from the overseas manufacturer, shipping contracts, air or sea waybills, customs entry summaries and quality inspection certificates; a treasury policy document that demonstrates a clear pattern of tiered supplier payments; bank reference letters from both the purchasing bank of the manufacturer and the account bank of the customer; and a three-month forward cash-flow projection aligned with purchase orders and inventory plans.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or loan capital to NZ_LTD from the non-resident parent or shareholders must be routed via an approved overseas bank and the New Zealand receiving bank using a standard SWIFT MT103 or an updated ISO 20022 payment message. The transferring bank must state a clear purpose code, typically 'Business-to-business trade' or 'Capital contribution', and the NZ beneficiary will be requested to present a board resolution, share subscription agreement or intercompany loan agreement, together with a funds-sourced declaration and, if applicable, an OIO approval or clearance certificate from the Overseas Investment Office. The receiving Tier 1 bank will credit the funds to a 'Capital Escrow Account' unless and until the commercial and legal documentation has been reviewed; upon confirmation of purpose, the funds are released to the primary operational account. These procedures satisfy the bank’s AMLCFT risk-based obligations and preserve clean audit trails for tax and capital reporting purposes. All capital injections will also be captured in the Reserve Bank’s Balance of Payments statistical survey where the bank determines direct investment reporting thresholds have been met.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For cross-border trade settlements — principally purchase of raw polyresin, pigments, packaging, and moulding accessories from overseas vendors — the recommended clearing rails are as follows: (i) high-value and irreconcilable trade payments use SWIFT MT103 messages with full purpose and invoice reference; (ii) documentary Letters of Credit, issued by the NZ opening bank under UCP 600 and confirmed by a correspondent bank, cover shipments from high-risk jurisdictions or for high-value manufacturing orders; (iii) for recurring payments below the bank’s de minimis threshold (typically NZD 50,000), the NZ_LTD may utilise the bank’s online electronic payment system to send NZD or foreign currency wires; and (iv) inbound customer settlements from Stripe and PayPal are collected via their NZ settlement mechanisms and swept to the operating account through white-label banking rails or direct API bank feeds. No exchange control approval is required for any outward remittance. The compliant payment file must contain the SWIFT code of the beneficiary bank, the beneficiary’s LEI or tax ID where available, the underlying commercial invoice, and the full legal entity name of the NZ_LTD, so that the bank can complete sanctions screening, AML travel-rule disclosure and regulatory reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign exchange forwards (up to 12 months, consummated for non-speculative hedging of trade and profit repatriation exposure)

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on illiquid or restricted-currency trade counterparties where physical settlement is not possible, provided the counterparty is a licensed New Zealand or reputable international bank
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) converting NZD-funded capital into USD or CNY for overseas investment, with prudent net exposure reporting
FX options (call and put spreads) used solely to hedge committed sales or procurement cash flows
Foreign exchange swap transactions (FX swaps) for short-term liquidity management between the operating account and the Bergen? no, between the NZD and USD/CNH accounts
Commodity-linked hedge instruments only for core polyresin input costs, structured as plain vanilla swaps, not speculative options

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 35 working days after the company's assigned annual return date; the annual return date is normally the anniversary of incorporation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The Registrar places the company in default; continued non-filing leads to a Notice of Intention to Remove and eventual strike-off from the New Zealand register. Directors may be fined up to NZD 10,000 for failing to provide required statutory information.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 is due by 7 July following the tax year end; an IRD-approved tax agent extension may apply. Terminal tax payment is due in accordance with the IRD assessment.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties and use-of-money interest apply under the Tax Administration Act 1994; persistent non-compliance may result in IRD default assessments, enforcement action against company assets, director liability notices, and prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial statements (prepared; filed only if required by size or ownership)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Prepared for shareholders; filed with the Companies Office only if the company is large, has 50 or more shareholders, is overseas-owned, or is subject to FMC reporting obligations.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after balance date if audited financial statements are required; otherwise prepared and distributed to shareholders in accordance with the Companies Act 1993 and the company's constitution.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may be subject to penalties and compensation orders for non-compliance; no filing penalty applies to a small exempt company.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit is compulsory unless the company qualifies as a small company under the Companies Act 1993 and is not otherwise required to be audited. The small-company test is met when at least two of the following apply: total assets not exceeding NZD 5 million, annual revenue not exceeding NZD 10 million, and fewer than 50 employees. An audit is also mandatory if the company is large under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, is an FMC reporting entity, or shareholders validly require an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (NZ GAAP), including NZ IFRS (Tier 1), NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (Tier 2), NZ small and medium entity accounting framework (Tier 3), or the simple format reporting framework (Tier 4), as set by the External Reporting Board (XRB).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Annual Return captures current shareholders and directors and is filed online with the Companies Office. There is no separate annual UBO filing form, but the company must continuously verify and record every beneficial owner with a controlling interest of 25% or more under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. Share transfers must be recorded in the Register of Members, and registry details must be true and current as at the annual return date.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book for directors' and shareholders' meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600–1,800 per annum for registered office and local agent service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 where the small-company exemption applies; approximately USD 8,000–20,000 for a certified audit engagement if required

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays or preferential corporate rate. Incentives: R&D Tax Incentive (15% credit on eligible R&D expenditure, with refundability for certain loss-making firms); tax losses deductible indefinitely (subject to continuity of ownership). No regional zone benefits in New Zealand.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (indefinite carryforward; subject to 49% continuity of ownership and same-business tests under s IA 5)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Company Income Tax Return; mandatory e-filing through IRD 'myIR' portal (and approved agents using EFILE)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; provisional tax (if required) paid in two or three instalments during the income year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Standard balance date (31 March): return due by 7 July (30 June for paper filers); non-standard balance date: due on the 7th day of the 6th month after the balance date (e.g., 30 June balance date due 7 January)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: IRD number, legal entity name, balance date and tax agent details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the company IRD number exactly as issued; for a non-resident-owned NZ company indicate the overseas parent/shareholder details in the related party schedule if applicable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from resin statue sales, licence fees and other business activity derived in New Zealand
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned NZ company must include all worldwide income because incorporation in NZ creates tax residency; apply transfer pricing to any purchases from related offshore suppliers; retain invoices, bills of lading and payment processor settlement records

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross interest earned from all sources, including bank deposits and intercompany loans
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report New Zealand-sourced interest gross; attach RWT credit certificates from NZ banks; apply thin capitalisation rules where interest deductions are paid to related non-resident lenders

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividends received from New Zealand and foreign companies, with imputation and foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a resident NZ company, dividends from NZ companies are excluded income if fully imputed; foreign dividends require assessment under the FIF rules and foreign tax credit calculations

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sum of all income boxes (Boxes 1 through 4)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure no double counting of imputed dividends or exempt income; non-resident-owned companies must reconcile gross sales against Stripe/PayPal settlement reports

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses: direct materials (polyresin, paint), licences, subcontract labour, shipping, merchant fees, insurance and overheads
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses incurred in deriving assessable income are deductible; capital costs (moulds, tooling) must be capitalised and depreciated; related-party payments must satisfy arm's length transfer pricing

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income less total expenses for the year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A net loss may be carried forward indefinitely if the 49% shareholder continuity test is met; a non-resident shareholder change can forfeit loss carryforward - check shareholders before offsetting

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax assessable at the 28% corporation rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute at flat 28% (no lower brackets for companies); do not apply the individual marginal tax tables; tax on taxable income cannot be reduced by shareholder tax credits at this box

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provisional tax paid, resident withholding tax on interest, imputation credits and other credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach copies of RWT and imputation credit statements; provisional tax credits must match instalment payments to avoid use-of-money interest; foreign tax credits are claimed on a separate schedule, not here

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Excess of tax assessed over credits, or refundable credit balance
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment is due on the terminal tax date (7 July for 31 March balance date); if a refund, IRD may hold it as a credit for next year unless overpayment is significant

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty (TAA s 139AA): NZ$250 immediately, plus NZ$250 if unfiled after one month. Late payment penalty (s 139A): 1% of the unpaid amount immediately, 4% after 7 days, then 1% per month (or part-month) thereafter. Use-of-money interest on underpayments (s 120E): 8.35% p.a. for the 2024-25 income year, compounding daily. Evasive failure to file may also trigger a 150% shortfall penalty and criminal prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on dividends paid to non-residents in the absence of any DTA relief
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced DTA rate, the non-resident shareholder must provide the NZ company with a completed Form IR1042 (Certificate of Residence) issued by the tax authority of the residence country before the dividend payment date. The NZ company must rely on the certificate, retain it for IRD audit, and apply the correct treaty rate (e.g., 15% under most NZ DTAs; Australia 15% generally, 5% for Australian resident pension funds). The recipient must be the beneficial owner; conduit companies without substance cannot claim treaty relief. The IRD may request a certificate of beneficial ownership and, where the dividend carries imputation credits, a supplementary dividend gross-up computation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory NRWT 15%; reduced to 10% under most treaties (e.g., Australia); alternatively, the Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) of 2% can apply to arm's-length interest paid to unassociated non-resident lenders where the NZ borrower is an approved issuer. Royalties: statutory NRWT 15%; treaty rates generally 10%–15% (Australia 10%; China 15%); definition follows ITA 2007 s RF 8, covering payments for the use of patents, designs, models, plans, and similar intellectual property.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory transfer pricing documentation (equivalent to Local File and Master File) is required when the taxpayer belongs to a multinational group with global group revenue exceeding NZ$1.2 billion (approx. EUR 750 million) AND cross-border related-party transactions in NZ aggregate NZ$10 million or more in an income year. Taxpayers below this threshold are still expected to maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing evidence under s GC 13 and may be required to produce it within 30 days on IRD notice.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not impose an Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime analogous to offshore financial centres. However, general anti-avoidance (s BG 1), thin capitalisation (s FE 1), and loss continuity rules (s IA 5) effectively require real economic substance. A NZ shell company with no employees, office, or decision-making, interposed to repatriate profits under DTA rates or to access NZ imputation credits, is vulnerable to IRD reconstruction, loss disallowance and penalty taxes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting NZ-source income (e.g., PayPal/Stripe revenue from resin statue sales to NZ buyers) from IR4; falsifying invoices or bank deposits; stripping profits to a related non-resident entity without transfer pricing documentation; claiming fictitious deductions for moulds, materials, or shipping.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil shortfall penalty under TAA s 141: 150% of the tax shortfall for evasion (100% for abusive tax position). Criminal prosecution under TAA s 143B: fine up to NZ$250,000 for a company (NZ$50,000 for an individual) and/or imprisonment up to 5 years. Use-of-money interest at 8.35% p.a. compounds daily on all unpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be made personally liable under TAA s 149 for unpaid tax if they knowingly caused the evasion; director liability also arises under Companies Act 1993 s 135 (reckless trading) and s 136 (insolvent trading). The Commissioner may issue a departure prohibition order under TAA s 157, preventing a director from leaving New Zealand until tax debts are settled.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The NZ company is used as a bare conduit for its non-resident owners: no local office, no employees, no local board meetings, no real management decisions; interposed solely to access NZ treaty benefits or to manufacture artificial losses; losses carried forward after a shareholding change without meeting the continuity test.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: General anti-avoidance rule (s BG 1) allows the Commissioner to reconstruct the arrangement and deny the tax benefit; loss carryforward denied under s IA 5; abusive tax position penalty of 100% of the shortfall. The company may be struck off under the Companies Act 1993 for failure to maintain a registered office or agent; banks and payment processors (Stripe/PayPal) may terminate accounts upon integrity review.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign falsely misleading returns commit an offence under TAA s 143A (knowingly providing false information) - fines up to NZ$50,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years. Directors may also incur civil liability for insolvent trading under Companies Act 1993 s 135/136 and personal liability for GST or PAYE collected but not remitted under TAA s 149.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / CFT and Payment Processor Integrity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The company accepts Stripe/PayPal preorder deposits for resin statues without maintaining beneficial-ownership records; allows pass-through of third-party funds; refuses to provide source-of-funds information to payment processors or the IRD; knowingly processes payments that are proceeds of crime or sanctions breaches.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Although the resin statue seller is not itself a reporting entity under the New Zealand AML/CFT Act 2009, knowingly dealing with the proceeds of crime constitutes money laundering under the Crimes Act 1961 s 243: imprisonment up to 7 years for individuals and fines for bodies corporate. The Crown may restrain and forfeit assets under the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009, and payment processors may permanently blacklist the entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be prosecuted for money laundering if they knew the funds were criminal proceeds, and personal civil penalties may arise under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2014 if preorders are materially misrepresented. Directors may also face travel bans, departure prohibition orders, and in serious cases simultaneous tax evasion and money laundering charges with cumulative imprisonment.
